Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.
Every finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space has an orthonormal basis. In dimension zero, this is the empty basis.

derivations.claim: For a nonzero vector, reshape its coefficient array as a matrix with row index $i_1$ and column index $(i_2,\ldots,i_N)$. By [F1] this gives an exact finite sum of products of a first-site coefficient and a residual coefficient array. Reshape the residual array at site $2$ with row index $(a_1,i_2)$ and remaining sites as column index, apply [F1] again, and store the resulting left coefficient array as the entries of $A_2^{i_2}$ with virtual indices $(a_1,a_2)$. Repeating this finite operation through site $N-1$ leaves a final array defining $A_N^{i_N}$; every SVD factorization is exact, so the original coefficient of each ordered product-basis vector is the displayed matrix product. For $N=1$ take the coefficients as scalar matrices. For the zero vector take all bond dimensions equal to $1$ and set the first site matrices to zero. For the nonzero construction choose each internal $D_j$ as the corresponding positive Schmidt rank; in both constructions use $D_0=D_N=1$ with $\ell=r=(1)$. Thus all finite vectors admit a representation with suitably chosen bond dimensions.

For any integer $q\ge1$ and positive semidefinite $Y\in M_q(\mathbb C)\otimes M_D(\mathbb C)$, the amplification is $({\rm id}_{M_q}\otimes\mathcal E)(Y)=\sum_{i=1}^d(I_q\otimes A^i)Y(I_q\otimes A^{i*})$. Each summand is positive semidefinite, so every amplification is positive and $\mathcal E$ is completely positive. The displayed definition also fixes its exact input and output spaces and makes no trace-preserving or unitality assertion.

The map $\Gamma_L$ is linear and its image is a finite-dimensional subspace of $(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes L}$. By [F2], choose an orthonormal basis $u_1,\ldots,u_s$ of that image and define $P_Lv:=\sum_{a=1}^s\langle v,u_a\rangle u_a$. Orthonormality gives $P_L^*=P_L$ and $P_L^2=P_L$, and $v-P_Lv$ is orthogonal to every $u_a$. Thus $h_L=I-P_L$ is the orthogonal projection onto the complement, with $\langle h_Lv,v\rangle=\|h_Lv\|^2\ge0$ and kernel $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$.

Fix a finite open MPS made from the same tensor and a block of $L$ consecutive sites. For each fixed physical-basis configuration outside that block, contraction of the outside tensors leaves a row $\alpha$ on the left and a column $\beta$ on the right. With $X=\beta\alpha$, direct coordinates give $\operatorname{tr}(XA^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L})=\sum_{u,v}\beta_u\alpha_v(A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L})_{vu}=\alpha A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L}\beta$, so that block slice is $\Gamma_L(X)$. The outside basis configurations are orthonormal, so the full vector is a sum of outside basis vectors tensored with block vectors in $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$; the corresponding $h_L$ therefore annihilates it. Each term in $H_{N,L}$ is positive semidefinite by step 1.3, and their sum annihilates the MPS. If that vector is nonzero, its normalized vector has quadratic form $0$, while every unit vector has nonnegative quadratic form; hence $E_0(H_{N,L})=0$, and it is a zero-energy ground-state vector by the Definition. The zero vector is annihilated but is excluded from ground-state vectors by definition. For example, if all tensor matrices vanish, then $\Gamma_L=0$, $h_L=I$ and $H_{N,L}=(N-L+1)I$, whose ground energy is positive. No uniqueness or positive-gap conclusion for a nonzero MPS follows from this argument.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $N\ge1$ and $d_1,\ldots,d_N,D_0,\ldots,D_N\ge1$ be integers. Give each site $j$ the Hilbert space $H_j=\mathbb C^{d_j}$ with standard inner product $\langle x,y\rangle:=\sum_{i=1}^{d_j}x_i\overline{y_i}$, linear in its first argument, and its fixed ordered standard basis $(|i_j\rangle)_{i_j=1}^{d_j}$. Tensor products use the ordered product basis and the product inner product. For every site and physical index choose a matrix $A_j^{i_j}\in M_{D_{j-1}\times D_j}(\mathbb C)$, a boundary column $\ell\in\mathbb C^{D_0}$, and a boundary column $r\in\mathbb C^{D_N}$. Here $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb C)$ is the space of $m$-by-$n$ complex matrices and $A^*$ denotes conjugate transpose. The associated finite open matrix product state (MPS) is the vector

$$|\psi_A\rangle:=\sum_{i_1=1}^{d_1}\cdots\sum_{i_N=1}^{d_N}\ell^*A_1^{i_1}\cdots A_N^{i_N}r\,|i_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes|i_N\rangle\in H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N.$$

The dimensions $D_j$ are the bond dimensions; the virtual indices between adjacent matrices are matrix indices summed in their product. The zero vector is allowed. A nonzero vector is normalized by division by its norm, and normalization is defined only when $\langle\psi_A,\psi_A\rangle>0$. Every vector in $H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$ has an exact open MPS representation for some choice of bond dimensions, with $D_0=D_N=1$ and $\ell=r=(1)$; the internal dimensions are chosen in the construction, rather than prescribed arbitrarily.

For a translation invariant tensor, let $d,D\ge1$ and use one family $A^i\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ for every site. Its transfer map is the completely positive linear map

$$\mathcal E:M_D(\mathbb C)\to M_D(\mathbb C),\qquad \mathcal E(X):=\sum_{i=1}^d A^iXA^{i*}.$$

Here complete positivity means that for every integer $q\ge1$, the amplified map $\operatorname{id}_{M_q}\otimes\mathcal E$ sends positive semidefinite matrices to positive semidefinite matrices; a matrix is positive semidefinite when it is Hermitian and has nonnegative quadratic form on every vector.

The tensor is injective at length $L\ge1$ when the matrices $A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L}$, over all $i_1,\ldots,i_L\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, span the full vector space $M_D(\mathbb C)$. No injectivity or transfer-spectrum condition is assumed by this definition.

For each block length $L\ge1$, define the blocked boundary map

$$\Gamma_L:M_D(\mathbb C)\to(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes L},\qquad \Gamma_L(X):=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_L=1}^d\operatorname{tr}(XA^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L})\,|i_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes|i_L\rangle,$$

where $\operatorname{tr}(Y):=\sum_{a=1}^D Y_{aa}$. Let $P_L$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$, set $h_L:=I-P_L$, and, for $N\ge L$, define the open-chain parent Hamiltonian

$$H_{N,L}:=\sum_{j=1}^{N-L+1}I^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes h_L\otimes I^{\otimes(N-j-L+1)}.$$

For a positive semidefinite operator $K$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional inner-product space, define its ground energy by

$$E_0(K):=\inf\{\langle Kv,v\rangle:\|v\|=1\}.$$

A **ground-state vector** of $K$ is a nonzero vector $\psi$ with $\langle K\psi,\psi\rangle/\|\psi\|^2=E_0(K)$. It is a **zero-energy ground-state vector** when $K\psi=0$; positivity then gives $E_0(K)=0$.

Each local term is positive semidefinite with kernel $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$, and $H_{N,L}$ annihilates every finite open MPS formed from the same translation invariant tensor. Every nonzero such vector is a zero-energy ground-state vector of $H_{N,L}$. This definition asserts no uniqueness of that ground state and no spectral-gap bound.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$, where $q$ is a positive integer (so $q\in\mathbb N$ and $1\le q$, by [[def-natural-numbers]] and [[def-nat-order]]). For $n\in\mathbb Z$, define $|n|=n$ if $0\le n$ and $|n|=-n$ if $n<0$, using the integer order and additive inverse of [[def-int-order]] and [[def-int-operations]]. Totality and compatibility of the integer order with addition ([[thm-int-ordered-ring]]) give $0\le|n|$ and $-|n|\le n\le|n|$. Adding these bounds for $m,n\in\mathbb Z$ gives $|m+n|\le|m|+|n|$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; the maximum exists because the coordinate set is finite and nonempty, symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the absolute-value triangle inequality gives $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate, hence the triangle inequality for $d_\infty$. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$ ([[def-finite-cardinality]]).

For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$. Induction on $|\Lambda|$ gives $|S_\Lambda|=q^{|\Lambda|}$: the empty region has one configuration, and for $x\in\Lambda$ the restriction map $s\mapsto(s|_{\Lambda\setminus\{x\}},s(x))$ is a bijection $S_\Lambda\to S_{\Lambda\setminus\{x\}}\times\{1,\ldots,q\}$, so adjoining one site multiplies the number of configurations by $q$, according to the recursion defining natural-number powers in [[def-nat-power]]. Let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis. For $\Lambda=\varnothing$, $S_\Lambda$ is a singleton and $\mathcal H_\Lambda\cong\mathbb C$. The **local spin matrix algebra** is

$$\mathcal A_\Lambda:=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)\cong M_{q^{|\Lambda|}}(\mathbb C),$$

Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional Hilbert space; they are bounded. The algebra has composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity $I_\Lambda$, and induced operator norm

$$\|T\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|T\xi\|.$$

The **finite local trace** is $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(T):=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}\langle T e_s,e_s\rangle$ in the displayed configuration basis $(e_s)$. This is the usual finite-matrix trace; basis independence and its cyclic/unitary identities are supplied by [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]].

If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, restriction of configurations gives the canonical factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$, with sites ordered lexicographically. The **factor inclusion** is the unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$ given by $T\mapsto T\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. A **localization region** for $T$ is any finite $\Lambda$ for which $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ under these inclusions; a localization region need not be minimal.

The ordinary operator norm makes each local matrix algebra a nonzero unital complete C*-algebra, and every positive normalized complex-linear functional is uniquely a trace pairing with a density matrix, by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. This includes the empty region, whose Hilbert space is $\mathbb C$. This definition does not posit an infinite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert space.

Use the finite local matrix algebras and isometric factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric]]. Identify $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ with its image in every larger finite-region algebra. The directed union

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$$

is the algebra of **strictly local observables**. Its norm is $\|A\|=\|A\|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ for any finite localization region $\Lambda$ of $A$; isometric inclusions make this independent of the chosen region. The **quasi-local spin algebra** is the norm completion

$$\mathcal A:=\overline{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.$$

The C*-algebra structure on this completion has product and adjoint extended continuously from the finite local matrix algebras. Countable Choice is assumed for the published existence theorem for metric completions; [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]] supplies the full extension argument using the finite C*-identity of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]].

**No global Hilbert tensor product is selected.** “Quasi-local” means norm completion of the directed algebra of finite-region observables; it does not mean a chosen representation as operators on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space. A local operator $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ may have more than one localization region. Disjoint finite local factors commute in their common finite tensor algebra.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $D=\dim H\ge1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. With composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity and the induced operator norm, $\mathcal B(H)$ is a nonzero unital complex C*-algebra in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. In particular it is complete, $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\|B\|$, $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$, $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ and $\|I\|=1$. The matrix $\|A\|^2I-A^*A$ is positive semidefinite and has a positive square root in $\mathcal B(H)$.

Every complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal B(H)\to\mathbb C$ that is positive, meaning $\omega(B^*B)\ge0$ for all $B$, has a unique positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ such that $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ for all $A$. It is bounded and satisfies

$$|\omega(A)|\le\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)\|A\|\quad(A\in\mathcal B(H)),\qquad \|\omega\|=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=\omega(I).$$

Consequently the canonical states of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]] are exactly the trace pairings of density operators of [[def-qc-density-operator]]; for a positive functional, normalization $\omega(I)=1$ is equivalent to norm one. The result includes zero positive functionals, nonfaithful densities and $D=1$; it makes no infinite-dimensional density representation assertion.

Let $\mathcal A$ be the unital quasi-local spin C*-algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], whose C*-structure uses Countable Choice as in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. An **infinite algebraic state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ satisfying $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$.

For each finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$, the restriction $\omega|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ is a finite-matrix state. By [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], every positive normalized functional on a finite matrix algebra is represented by a unique density matrix. Define its **local density matrix** $\rho_\Lambda$ by

$$\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda),$$

where $\rho_\Lambda=\rho_\Lambda^*\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}\rho_\Lambda=1$. For $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, put $\Delta=\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda$ and use the configuration-basis factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_\Delta$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. If $T\in\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$, define its **partial trace over $\Delta$**, $\operatorname{Tr}_\Delta(T)\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, by its matrix coefficients

$$\langle \operatorname{Tr}_\Delta(T)e_s,e_{s'}\rangle:=\sum_{t\in S_\Delta}\langle T(e_s\otimes e_t),e_{s'}\otimes e_t\rangle\qquad(s,s'\in S_\Lambda),$$

where $e_s$ and $e_t$ are the configuration basis vectors of $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ and $\mathcal H_\Delta$. The finite sums depend linearly on $T$, so they define a linear map $\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}\to\mathcal A_\Lambda$ with a unique output matrix for each $T$. Expanding both configuration-basis traces gives its pairing identity

$$\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda\!\left(A\operatorname{Tr}_\Delta(T)\right)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'}\!\left((A\otimes I_\Delta)T\right)\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda),$$

with the common value given by

$$\sum_{s,s'\in S_\Lambda}\sum_{t\in S_\Delta}\langle A e_{s'},e_s\rangle\langle T(e_s\otimes e_t),e_{s'}\otimes e_t\rangle.$$

The pairing identity determines this matrix uniquely: if $D\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ pairs to zero with every $A$, taking the configuration-basis matrix units $A=E_{ji}$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(E_{ji}D)=\langle D e_j,e_i\rangle=0$ for every $i,j$, so $D=0$. The local densities are **consistent** when $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$. No density operator on a globally chosen Hilbert space is part of this definition.

This agrees with the canonical state convention of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]: the finite restrictions have norm one by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], giving $|\omega(A)|\le\|A\|$ on the dense local algebra and hence on its completion; evaluation at the norm-one identity gives $\|\omega\|=1$. Conversely a canonical state has local restrictions with density matrices of trace one, since the finite norm formula and continuity on the dense local algebra imply $\|\omega\|=\omega(I)$. No global density representation is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice for the norm completion in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be positive trace-one matrices, one on each finite-region algebra $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], such that for every $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$ their partial traces agree: $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$. There is a unique infinite algebraic state $\omega$ on $\mathcal A$ whose restriction to each $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ is $A\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)$.

Use the following conventions on a complex inner-product space $H$ of dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. For an endomorphism $A$, define $\operatorname{Tr}A:=\sum_{j=1}^D\langle Ae_j,e_j\rangle$ in an orthonormal basis; step 3.1 proves basis independence. For any Hermitian $M$, its **positive spectral subspace** (called its positive support here) is $S_M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda>0}\ker(M-\lambda I)$; when $M\geq0$ this equals $(\ker M)^\perp$. Its support logarithm is $\log(M|_{S_M}):=\sum_{\lambda>0}(\log\lambda)P_\lambda|_{S_M}$, where $P_\lambda$ is the orthogonal projection onto that eigenspace. No value $\log0$ is assigned; for $M=0$ this is the unique endomorphism of the zero space. For the set $\mathcal D(H)$ of positive semidefinite Hermitian endomorphisms with trace one, a point $\rho$ is **extreme** if every equality $\rho=t\sigma+(1-t)\tau$ with $\sigma,\tau\in\mathcal D(H)$ and $0<t<1$ implies $\sigma=\tau=\rho$.

Let $H$ be a complex inner-product space of finite dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. Every Hermitian endomorphism $M$ has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues. For a real function $f$ on its finite spectrum, define $f(M)$ by its spectral projections; this definition is independent of the choice of eigenbasis. In particular positive square roots, exponentials, and logarithms on positive supports are well defined.

For a density matrix $\rho$ on $H$, meaning a Hermitian positive semidefinite operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\sum_jp_j\langle Au_j,u_j\rangle$ for bounded $A$, where $\rho=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$. The weighted form $(X,Y)_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X^*Y)$ satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz, $|(X,Y)_\rho|^2\leq(X,X)_\rho(Y,Y)_\rho$. Finally, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2)\leq1$, with equality exactly for rank-one densities, and those are exactly the extreme points of the finite density-matrix set.

derivations.claim: The finite coefficient sum defining $\mathcal E_O(X)$ is complex-linear in both $O$ and $X$. For $O\ge0$, write its spectral decomposition as $O=\sum_\alpha|v_\alpha\rangle\langle v_\alpha|$, absorbing the square roots of the nonnegative eigenvalues into $v_\alpha$, and put $v_{\alpha,I}=\langle v_\alpha,e_I\rangle$. Then $O_{I,J}=\sum_\alpha v_{\alpha,I}\overline{v_{\alpha,J}}$, so with $K_\alpha:=\sum_J\overline{v_{\alpha,J}}A^J$ the insertion map satisfies $\mathcal E_O(X)=\sum_\alpha K_\alpha X K_\alpha^*\ge0$ whenever $X\ge0$. Diagonalizing $\ell$ by [F7] and expanding $\operatorname{tr}(\ell\mathcal E_O(\rho))$ as a weighted sum of nonnegative diagonal expectations shows $\omega_k(O)\ge0$. For $O=I_{d^k}$, $O_{I,J}=1$ if $I=J$ and $0$ otherwise, so the insertion sums over all length-$k$ words and equals $\mathcal E^k$. The fixed-point equations and $\operatorname{tr}(\ell\rho)=1$ give $\omega_k(I)=\operatorname{tr}(\ell\mathcal E^k(\rho))=1$. Thus each contiguous-block functional is positive and normalized.

Tensor-factor order in the definition gives $\mathcal E_{O\otimes P}=\mathcal E_O\circ\mathcal E_P$ for consecutive blocks: expanding both sides gives the same ordered product $A^{J_O}A^{J_P}X(A^{I_P})^*(A^{I_O})^*$. Inserting an identity site on the right composes with $\mathcal E$ on the input, which leaves $\rho$ fixed; inserting one on the left composes with $\mathcal E$ on the output, which leaves the trace pairing with $\ell$ fixed. Repeating these identities shows that the value is independent of the chosen containing interval and that restrictions to nested finite regions agree. A positive observable remains positive when identity factors are inserted, so the local functionals on arbitrary finite regions are positive and normalized as well. The empty-region convention is consistent because every local functional assigns one to the identity.

By [F2]–[F4] each local positive normalized functional has a unique trace-one density $\rho_\Lambda$. For nested regions, step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{tr}_{\Lambda'}((O\otimes I)\rho_{\Lambda'})=\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(O\rho_\Lambda)$ for every $O\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$. Applying the defining partial-trace pairing [F5] shows $\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(O\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'}))=\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(O\rho_\Lambda)$ for all $O$. Taking $O$ to be each matrix unit makes every matrix entry of the two matrices equal, so the density family is consistent.

Apply [F6] to the consistent finite-region density family from step 3.1. Its hypotheses hold by [A1], [F2], [F3], and the positive trace-one property just proved. It yields a unique infinite algebraic state on the specified quasi-local algebra, with exactly these local restrictions and no chosen global Hilbert-space representation. This establishes that the transfer contractions in the Definition are well defined.

Input an integer $N\ge1$, nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_1,\ldots,H_N$ with fixed ordered orthonormal bases, a normalized vector $\psi\in H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$ with exact coefficients in those bases, and integer rank caps $D_k\ge1$ for $1\le k<N$. For $N=1$ the cap list is empty. The algorithm performs the following exact finite procedure.

1. Set the current remainder to $\psi^{(0)}:=\psi$, the retained left space before the first cut to $S_0:=\mathbb C$, and an empty list of site tensors and discarded squared norms.

2. For each $k=1,\ldots,N-1$, reshape the current remainder as a matrix whose row index is the retained left index in $S_{k-1}$ together with the physical basis index in $H_k$, and whose column index is the ordered product basis of $H_{k+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$. Compute an exact singular value decomposition. Order the positive singular values nonincreasingly. Within each repeated positive singular value, form a deterministic orthonormal basis of its left singular subspace by projecting the row-coordinate standard basis vectors in lexicographic order and applying Gram–Schmidt, discarding zero residuals; obtain the corresponding right singular vector as $M^*u/s$ for singular value $s>0$. where $\lambda_j$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho$, the logarithm is natural, and $0\log0:=0$. For any positive semidefinite endomorphisms $X,Y$ on one finite-dimensional $H$, let $\operatorname{supp}X:=(\ker X)^\perp$. Define

$$D(X\|Y):=\operatorname{Tr}(X\log X)-\operatorname{Tr}(X\log Y)$$

when $\operatorname{supp}X\subseteq\operatorname{supp}Y$, taking each logarithm spectrally on its positive support and setting zero-eigenvalue contributions to zero; set $D(X\|Y):=+\infty$ otherwise. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy in nats.

$$I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a density operator $\rho_{ABC}$ on $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, define

$$\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_C\rho_{ABC},\qquad \rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{ABC},\qquad \rho_B:=\operatorname{Tr}_A(\operatorname{Tr}_C\rho_{ABC}),$$

where each partial trace contracts the indicated tensor factor and retains the other factors in their displayed order.

$$I(A:C\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{ABC}),$$

using the partial traces in the displayed factor order. For any fixed positive conversion factor $k_B$ with units J/K, the corresponding physical entropy is $S_{\mathrm{phys}}(\rho):=k_BS(\rho)$; no numerical value of $k_B$ is specified here.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ (Continuity of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point of $A$ and on $A$: the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, its agreement with $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ at a limit point, and continuity at an isolated point, Intervals of $\mathbb{R}$: the nine order-convex forms, nondegeneracy, and length) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
(The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

derivations.claim: Since $\|\psi\|=1$ and every cap $D_k\ge1$, each current remainder has a positive singular value and the algorithm retains at least one; hence all subsequent remainders are nonzero and all retained bond dimensions are positive. The loop makes one SVD for each $k=1,\ldots,N-1$, exactly $N-1$ in total. Put $\mathcal H_{\le k}:=H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_k$ and $\mathcal R_k:=H_{k+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$, with $\mathcal H_{\le0}=\mathbb C$. Let $U_k:S_k\to S_{k-1}\otimes H_k$ have the retained left singular columns, so $U_k^*U_k=I_{S_k}$ and $\psi^{(k)}=(U_k^*\otimes I_{\mathcal R_k})\psi^{(k-1)}$. Define $W_0=I_{\mathbb C}$ and $W_k=(W_{k-1}\otimes I_{H_k})U_k:S_k\to\mathcal H_{\le k}$. Each $W_k$ is an isometry by induction. Under the canonical $\mathbb C\otimes\mathcal H\cong\mathcal H$ identification, set $x_0=\psi$, $P_0=I$, and, for $k\ge1$, $x_k=(W_k\otimes I_{\mathcal R_k})\psi^{(k)}$ and $P_k=(W_kW_k^*)\otimes I_{\mathcal R_k}$ on the full chain. The range of $W_k$ lies in $\operatorname{ran}W_{k-1}\otimes H_k$, so $\operatorname{ran}P_k\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_{k-1}$ and $P_kP_{k-1}=P_{k-1}P_k=P_k$. The remainder recurrence gives $x_k=P_kx_{k-1}=P_k\psi$ inductively. Expanding $W_{N-1}$ in the stored site tensors shows that $x_{N-1}$ is exactly their contraction with the final remainder, hence is the returned unnormalized $\phi$ in algorithm instruction 3. For $N=1$, $x_0=\phi=\psi$.

Across cut $k$, the coefficient matrix of an exact MPS factors as $L_kR_k$ by summing over its $D_k$-dimensional virtual index. Its matrix rank is therefore at most $D_k$. By [F3]–[F4], the Schmidt rank is the number of positive singular values, so it is at most $D_k$. Writing the Schmidt expansion as $\psi=\sum_{j=1}^q s_j u_j\otimes v_j$ gives $q\le D_k$, $p_j:=s_j^2>0$, and $\sum_jp_j=1$. Expanding the partial trace in [F5] gives $\rho_{1\cdots k}=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$, so these $p_j$ are exactly its positive eigenvalues.

Put $\varepsilon_k:=x_{k-1}-x_k=(P_{k-1}-P_k)\psi$ in the full chain. This vector lies in $\operatorname{ran}P_{k-1}$ and is orthogonal to $\operatorname{ran}P_k$. For $j>k$, nesting gives $\varepsilon_j\in\operatorname{ran}P_{j-1}\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_k$, so $\langle\varepsilon_k,\varepsilon_j\rangle=0$. Thus the embedded discarded components from different cuts are pairwise orthogonal.

At cut $k$, $\varepsilon_k=(W_{k-1}\otimes I_{H_k\otimes \mathcal R_k})(\psi^{(k-1)}-(U_k\otimes I_{\mathcal R_k})\psi^{(k)})$. The map outside the parentheses is an isometry by step 1.1, and the vector in parentheses is the discarded Schmidt part of the current compressed remainder. Hence [F3] and [F1] give $\|\varepsilon_k\|^2=\delta_k$. Since $x_0=\psi$ and $x_{N-1}=\phi$, telescoping gives $\psi-\phi=\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}\varepsilon_k$; orthogonality from step 2.1 yields $\|\psi-\phi\|^2=\sum_k\|\varepsilon_k\|^2=\sum_k\delta_k$. For $N=1$ both sides are zero, so the equality also covers the empty sweep.

For every $x>1$, apply [F8] to $\log$ on $[1,x]$; [F6]–[F7] give $\log x=(x-1)/c\le x-1$ for some $c\in(1,x)$. For $0<x<1$, apply [F8] on $[x,1]$ to get $-\log x=(1-x)/c$ for some $c\in(x,1)$, hence $\log x\le x-1$; equality holds at $x=1$. Apply this inequality to $x=(q p_j)^{-1}$, multiply by $p_j>0$, and sum: $\sum_jp_j\log((q p_j)^{-1})\le\sum_j(1/q-p_j)=0$. The logarithm product law [F6] then gives $\log q-S(\rho_{1\cdots k})=\sum_jp_j\log(qp_j)\ge0$. Since $q\le D_k$ and $\log$ is increasing, $S(\rho_{1\cdots k})\le\log q\le\log D_k$. The zero-eigenvalue convention in [F5] includes rank-deficient reductions.

$$T(v)=\lambda v.$$

$$E_\lambda(T):=\ker(T-\lambda I_V)=\{v\in V:T(v)=\lambda v\}.$$

$$\sigma_F(T):=\{\lambda\in F:\lambda\text{ is an eigenvalue of }T\}.$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $N\ge1$ and $d_1,\ldots,d_N,D_0,\ldots,D_N\ge1$ be integers. Give each site $j$ the Hilbert space $H_j=\mathbb C^{d_j}$ with standard inner product $\langle x,y\rangle:=\sum_{i=1}^{d_j}x_i\overline{y_i}$, linear in its first argument, and its fixed ordered standard basis $(|i_j\rangle)_{i_j=1}^{d_j}$. Tensor products use the ordered product basis and the product inner product. For every site and physical index choose a matrix $A_j^{i_j}\in M_{D_{j-1}\times D_j}(\mathbb C)$, a boundary column $\ell\in\mathbb C^{D_0}$, and a boundary column $r\in\mathbb C^{D_N}$. Here $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb C)$ is the space of $m$-by-$n$ complex matrices and $A^*$ denotes conjugate transpose. The associated finite open matrix product state (MPS) is the vector

$$|\psi_A\rangle:=\sum_{i_1=1}^{d_1}\cdots\sum_{i_N=1}^{d_N}\ell^*A_1^{i_1}\cdots A_N^{i_N}r\,|i_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes|i_N\rangle\in H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N.$$

The dimensions $D_j$ are the bond dimensions; the virtual indices between adjacent matrices are matrix indices summed in their product. The zero vector is allowed. A nonzero vector is normalized by division by its norm, and normalization is defined only when $\langle\psi_A,\psi_A\rangle>0$. Every vector in $H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$ has an exact open MPS representation for some choice of bond dimensions, with $D_0=D_N=1$ and $\ell=r=(1)$; the internal dimensions are chosen in the construction, rather than prescribed arbitrarily.

For a translation invariant tensor, let $d,D\ge1$ and use one family $A^i\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ for every site. Its transfer map is the completely positive linear map

$$\mathcal E:M_D(\mathbb C)\to M_D(\mathbb C),\qquad \mathcal E(X):=\sum_{i=1}^d A^iXA^{i*}.$$

Here complete positivity means that for every integer $q\ge1$, the amplified map $\operatorname{id}_{M_q}\otimes\mathcal E$ sends positive semidefinite matrices to positive semidefinite matrices; a matrix is positive semidefinite when it is Hermitian and has nonnegative quadratic form on every vector.

The tensor is injective at length $L\ge1$ when the matrices $A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L}$, over all $i_1,\ldots,i_L\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, span the full vector space $M_D(\mathbb C)$. No injectivity or transfer-spectrum condition is assumed by this definition.

For each block length $L\ge1$, define the blocked boundary map

$$\Gamma_L:M_D(\mathbb C)\to(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes L},\qquad \Gamma_L(X):=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_L=1}^d\operatorname{tr}(XA^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L})\,|i_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes|i_L\rangle,$$

where $\operatorname{tr}(Y):=\sum_{a=1}^D Y_{aa}$. Let $P_L$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$, set $h_L:=I-P_L$, and, for $N\ge L$, define the open-chain parent Hamiltonian

$$H_{N,L}:=\sum_{j=1}^{N-L+1}I^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes h_L\otimes I^{\otimes(N-j-L+1)}.$$

For a positive semidefinite operator $K$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional inner-product space, define its ground energy by

$$E_0(K):=\inf\{\langle Kv,v\rangle:\|v\|=1\}.$$

A **ground-state vector** of $K$ is a nonzero vector $\psi$ with $\langle K\psi,\psi\rangle/\|\psi\|^2=E_0(K)$. It is a **zero-energy ground-state vector** when $K\psi=0$; positivity then gives $E_0(K)=0$.

Each local term is positive semidefinite with kernel $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$, and $H_{N,L}$ annihilates every finite open MPS formed from the same translation invariant tensor. Every nonzero such vector is a zero-energy ground-state vector of $H_{N,L}$. This definition asserts no uniqueness of that ground state and no spectral-gap bound.

Fix integers $d,D\ge1$ and a translation invariant tensor $A^1,\ldots,A^d\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ with transfer map $\mathcal E(X):=\sum_iA^iXA^{i*}$. A matrix is positive semidefinite when it is Hermitian with nonnegative quadratic form on every vector. Let $\rho,\ell\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ be positive semidefinite matrices satisfying

$$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1,\qquad \mathcal E(\rho)=\rho,\qquad \mathcal E^*(\ell)=\ell,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\ell\rho)=1,$$

where $\mathcal E^*(Y):=\sum_iA^{i*}YA^i$, equivalently the trace-pairing adjoint determined by $\operatorname{tr}(Y\mathcal E(X))=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal E^*(Y)X)$. For a contiguous block of $k\ge1$ sites, write $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_k)$ for physical multi-indices, let $e_I$ be its ordered standard product basis, put $O_{I,J}:=\langle Oe_J,e_I\rangle$ for $O\in M_{d^k}(\mathbb C)$, and set $A^I:=A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_k}$. Define the transfer insertion map and local expectation by

$$\mathcal E_O(X):=\sum_{I,J}O_{I,J}A^JX(A^I)^*,\qquad \omega_k(O):=\operatorname{tr}(\ell\mathcal E_O(\rho)).$$

For any finite nonempty $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z$ and local observable $O\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, embed $O$ into the interval $[\min\Lambda,\max\Lambda]$ by inserting identities at missing sites and evaluate the same formula. For the empty region set $\omega_\varnothing(cI):=c$. These definitions give compatible positive normalized local functionals. Their unique density matrices $\rho_\Lambda$ obey $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$ whenever $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$. Assume Countable Choice. The transfer-generated infinite-chain state is the unique infinite algebraic state $\omega$ on the norm-completed quasi-local spin algebra whose restriction to every finite region is the defined local functional. No infinite tensor-product Hilbert space is selected.

For observables $O_A\in M_{d^a}(\mathbb C)$ and $O_B\in M_{d^b}(\mathbb C)$ on two fixed consecutive blocks, with $g\ge0$ identity sites between the blocks, the connected correlation is

$$\omega(O_A\otimes I^{\otimes g}\otimes O_B)-\omega(O_A)\omega(O_B).$$
